bindings.identity_reason: The focal arrangement is referentially identified as the alleged subletting of the disputed shop by the respondent to Kapil Luthra. The respondent's denial expressly repeats Kapil's name, the shop and the challenged subletting, providing a source-based connection between the opposing accounts. The absence of the respondent's personal name does not make the litigating respondent a different actor across these directly corresponding pleadings. This establishes the identity of the disputed arrangement at the pleaded level, without establishing subletting, assignment, rent, exclusive possession or any other substantive test. The separately quoted unidentified client in B2 is not thereby identified as this respondent.

coverage_limits: All 31 original limitation IDs are mapped. All 17 old links are assigned once.
The petitioner and respondent accounts of the Kapil Luthra shop arrangement are retained together in B1 as conflicting accounts, not incorrectly split into separate transactions.
B2 isolates the unidentified client statement without claiming that it proves an independent real-world transaction.
The respondent's name is not inferred merely from repeated litigation-role labels or legacy entity IDs.
The alleged Rs.5500 monthly rent and exclusive possession remain allegations; respondent-side denials and family-help accounts remain contested statements.
The alleged disposition date is unknown; the absence of a date affects C01 without extinguishing other event descriptions.
Landlord knowledge of godown use is not converted into consent or written consent.
The supplied oral-partnership and business-use snippets with unidentified speakers are not re-extracted as additional decisive transactions.
C06 applies only to the parting-with-possession route.
The law leaves proof burdens and standards NOT_COVERED, without automatically barring any facts.
All material remains at its supplied pre-target retrospective status; no eviction outcome is predicted.
